sources.claim: Tennessee's ELVIS Act (signed March 21, 2024; effective July 1, 2024) added a person's voice, including a simulated voice, to the state's right of publicity, with liability for unauthorized commercial use and for certain tools whose main purpose is imitating a specific person.

FCC Declaratory Ruling (February 8, 2024): AI-generated voices in calls count as "artificial" voices under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, so such calls need the same prior consent and disclosures as other prerecorded calls.

sections.skill: Explain voice cloning and why consent and disclosure matter

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What is voice cloning?

choices.text: Recording someone's voice once and playing back exactly the same recording many times
Making music from noise
Making a synthetic voice that sounds like a real person
Turning speech into text

questions.correct_answer: Making a synthetic voice that sounds like a real person
questions.intro: VOICE CLONING uses recordings of a real person to make a synthetic voice that sounds like them saying new words. It has real uses, such as helping people who are losing their voice, but it can also fool listeners: scam calls, fake endorsements, or false statements. CONSENT (the person agrees) and DISCLOSURE (listeners are told the voice is synthetic) matter. Some laws now address this. Tennessee's ELVIS Act (effective July 1, 2024) added a person's voice, including a simulated one, to that state's publicity rights. In February 2024, the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) ruled that AI-generated voices in calls count as "artificial" voices that need prior consent.

sections.skill: Compare voice cloning with borrowing someone's signature

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: Why does a signature matter?

choices.text: Because it is written in ink
Because signatures are always the most beautiful part of any written document
Because it shows your height
People believe you agreed when they see it

questions.correct_answer: People believe you agreed when they see it
questions.intro: Your SIGNATURE stands for you: when people see it, they believe you agreed. Copying someone's signature without permission to sign a document would be wrong, even if the copy is perfect. A cloned VOICE works similarly: listeners believe the person is speaking. Using it with their CONSENT, and saying it is synthetic, is like signing with permission and a note. Using it without consent to fool people is like forging a signature.

sections.skill: Navigate differing laws and protect against voice scams

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: A voice use is allowed in one state. Is it allowed everywhere?

choices.text: Not necessarily; laws differ by place
Yes, if it is online
No, it is banned everywhere
Yes, because every state and every country follows exactly the same rules about voices

questions.correct_answer: Not necessarily; laws differ by place
questions.intro: Laws on voices differ by place and are still developing, so a use allowed in one state or country may not be allowed in another, and courts are still deciding many questions. Practical rules hold everywhere: get clear written permission before cloning someone's voice, say when audio is synthetic, never imitate a real person to deceive, and be suspicious of urgent calls that "sound like" a relative asking for money. Families can agree on a code word to verify each other on the phone.
